newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak support for EU membership grows again.
newsitem.headline: Slovak support for EU membership grows again.

text.p: Support for European Union (EU) membership has risen again this year, almost hitting the high point reached in 1995, according to a poll by the independent public opinion agency Focus released on Thursday.
The survey conducted in mid-September showed support for EU membership had risen to 58.5 percent from 52.8 percent in April and stood only slightly below the peak of 58.8 percent hit last year.
Focus said 10.3 percent of 1,007 respondents polled would have voted against EU membership in a referendum compared with 13.6 percent in April.
But the number of those who would not vote in a referendum grew to 19.7 percent from 18.3 percent, while the percentage of those undecided fell to 11.5 from 15.3.
Slovakia applied formally for EU membership in June 1995. It has replied to a detailed Brussels questionnaire which will be the basis for assessing new applicants.
EU member states are in the middle of an inter-governmental conference (IGC) which includes plotting the shape of an expanded union.

But officials say even the most ardent supporters now accept the most likely first batch of new members -- Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and possibly Slovenia -- are unlikely to gain admission before 2002.

Slovakia is seen as being on the edge of the first wave of possible candidates after four EU ambassadors handed a diplomatic note to Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar expressing worry about Bratislava's failure to follow democratic norms for joining the Union.
